subject: Persistent socket profiles & quota handoff for FinFlow pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrova <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — persistent sockets, concurrency profile, next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size the pilot quota correctly.

Summary of what I heard from FinFlow:
- Primary flow: real-time underwriting checks that use a streaming response for policy generation (avg response 350 tokens).
- Expected peak concurrent sessions: ~1,200 (users concurrently in a short window).
- Within each session: up to 2–3 parallel inference requests (RPS spikes when they fetch related attributes).
- Bursts: occasional 10–15 minute marketing spikes where total parallel requests can hit ~1,800.
- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for prompt+response on a 512-token context (business-critical).
- Prefer persistent socket reuse (long-lived HTTP/2 or websocket) from their front-end to reduce TLS churn and lower p99 tail latency.

Open items we need from FinFlow to finalize quota:
1) Confirm whether the persistent connections will be per user (1 socket/session) or pooled by their edge (1 socket per N users).
2) Clarify whether the streaming responses are multiplexed over a single socket per session or open separate connections per request.
3) Any regulatory constraints on token retention (for caching/KV cache policies).

Ben & Marissa — I flagged this for a quota proposal because the combination of persistent sockets + parallel requests + burst behavior pushes them into a higher connection-concurrency tier. I attached the load spec FinFlow shared (finflow-load-specs.pdf) and a CSV template for how we expect connection/session counts (redwood-conn-profile.csv).

Next steps proposed:
- Aisha to confirm the 3 items above (by end of day Thursday).
- We'll provision a tentative pilot quota and a small canary window (3 days) while we validate latency SLOs.
- Technical onboarding with Aditya for kernel/hardening recommendations during the canary.

Thanks — O.

--
Olga Petrova
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
redwood.ai
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finflow.com>
To: Olga Petrova <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finflow.com>, support@finflow.com
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — persistent sockets, concurrency profile, next steps

Thanks Olga — great summary. Answers inline.

> Confirm whether the persistent connections will be per user (1 socket/session) or pooled by their edge

We will run persistent sockets per front-end edge instance (we have a small number of edge pools). Each edge instance will multiplex requests for thousands of users; in practice we expect ~300 sockets from our edges to Redwood in steady state and up to ~1,400 sockets on peak (during spikes). We will not open a socket per end-user.

> Are streaming responses multiplexed over a single socket per session or separate connections per request

Streaming will be over the same socket where possible (HTTP/2 multiplexing). However some legacy clients fall back to separate websocket channels — we estimate those at ~5% of traffic.

> Token retention / caching constraints

We can permit short-lived KV caching for prefixes (30m) — we cannot persist any user-identifying data beyond session duration.

Load & latency expectations:
- Sustained throughput target: 600 RPS (inference requests)
- Burst profile: up to 1,800 parallel requests for 10–15 minutes, 2–3 times per week
- Concurrency per request: ~1.5 average parallelism (because many calls are single request, some fan-out)
- Latency SLA request: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms

We can share an anonymized traffic dump if you need per-route distributions.

Tom — looping you for any procurement constraints and to review the pilot addendum when ready.

Aisha
Director, Platform Engineering
FinFlow
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrova <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal — tentative quotas and rate model for FinFlow pilot

Folks — based on Aisha's numbers, here's a suggested starting configuration we can offer for the hosted pilot (we can move to Dedicated if they require stronger isolation). Biggest levers are persistent socket caps and concurrent request quota.

Proposal (pilot, 2-week canary + 1-month pilot):
- Connection pool (persistent sockets): soft cap 1,500 sockets, hard cap 1,800 sockets (to accommodate peaks).
- Concurrent in-flight request quota: baseline 2,400 concurrent requests; burstable to 3,600 for up to 15 minutes, 3x/week.
- Request throttling policy: token-bucket per connection + account-level circuit breaker. We'll configure a grace window during canary to avoid false positives.
- Streaming concurrency: prioritize pinned-serving lanes for streaming sessions to reduce head-of-line blocking; allocate 20% of capacity to streaming-preserved lanes.
- Latency targets: we will aim to meet their p95 <= 200ms on pilot hardware; if not achieved we'll iterate kernel/quant settings.

Commercial & ops notes:
- Pilot will carry a temporary quota uplift (monthly equivalent) while under validation. If they move to Reserved/Dedicated: we will migrate quotas to dedicated pools and remove burst restrictions.
- Need procurement to sign the pilot addendum (DocuSign link).
- Send them an onboarding checklist and a contact for SRE support during canary (Aditya).

I've attached a CSV with the connection/profile assumptions and a draft pilot addendum. Marissa — can you own pricing & procurement follow-up? I can handle the technical handoff.

- Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrova <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finflow.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — persistent sockets, concurrency profile, next steps

Aisha — thanks for the clear answers. Confirming next steps so we stay coordinated: 

1) Redwood will provision the pilot quota as Ben proposed: 1,500 soft socket cap / 1,800 hard, 2,400 baseline concurrency with 3,600 burst allowance.
2) Aditya will lead a 60-minute onboarding call next Tue (23 Aug) to validate routing/HTTP2 multiplexing behavior and recommend small kernel tweaks for streaming p95.
3) Marissa will send the pilot addendum and pricing rows via DocuSign today; Tom / procurement to review and sign.
4) Aisha to share the anonymized traffic dump or a 1-hour sample (S3 link or Drive) so we can validate batching/prefix cache impact.

We will lift some throttles during the 72-hour canary to minimize false positives. We will monitor p95/p99 and token economics closely and iterate the quota if we see sustained oversubscription.

Attachments: pilot-addendum-draft.docx (for signature), redwood-conn-profile.csv (connection assumptions), finflow-load-specs.pdf (your load spec).

If all good, I'll schedule the technical onboarding and mark the pilot kickoff as 2028-08-24 (tentative).

Thanks everyone — look forward to the canary.

Olga
